captions: Hello, and welcome to Camday English, Stage 5. In this lesson: Our solar system.
Read a non-fiction text with numbers and compare planets.
Here are some new words. Planet. A large round object that moves around a star. Orbit.
The path one object takes around another in space. Astronaut.
A person who travels into space. Listen and say them. planet
orbit
astronaut.
And some more words. Gravity. The force that pulls things towards each other. Atmosphere.
The layer of gases around a planet. Telescope. A tool that makes faraway things look closer.
Listen and say them. gravity
atmosphere
telescope.
Time for a question. The video will stop.
Which word means: a large round object that moves around a star?
Now some grammar: Comparing with as, as, and not as, as. Use as, plus an adjective, plus as,
to show two things are the same, and not as, as, to show they are different.
For example: Venus is almost as big as Earth. For example: Mars is not as hot as Venus.
Now listen, and read along. The planets in our solar system.
Eight planets orbit the Sun in our solar system.
The four closest to the Sun – Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars – are small and rocky.
Venus is the hottest planet. Its thick atmosphere traps heat,
so it is even hotter than Mercury, which is closer to the Sun.
The four outer planets – Jupiter, Saturn,
Uranus and Neptune – are giant planets made mostly of gas and ice.
Jupiter is so big that more than 1,000 Earths could fit inside it.
Earth is the only planet where we know life exists. It has liquid water,
air we can breathe and a temperature that is not too hot and not too cold.
Another question. The video will stop. How many planets orbit the Sun?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like planet, orbit, astronaut.
You practised comparing with as, as. And you read The planets in our solar system.
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!

captions: Hello, and welcome to Camday English, Stage 5. In this lesson: Should we live on Mars?
Report what people said and understand a balanced discussion.
Here are some new words. Discussion. A text or talk that gives different points of view.
Argument. A reason why you think something is right or wrong. Expensive.
Costing a lot of money. Listen and say them. discussion
argument
expensive.
And some more words. Survive. Stay alive in a difficult situation. Explore.
Travel to find out about a new place. Conclusion. The end part that gives a final opinion.
Listen and say them. survive
explore
conclusion.
Time for a question. The video will stop.
Which word means: a text or talk that gives different points of view?
Now some grammar: Reported speech. When we report what someone said,
the verb usually moves one step into the past: is becomes was, can becomes could,
will becomes would.
For example: ‘Mars is cold,’ she said, becomes: She said that Mars was cold.
For example: ‘We can go,’ he said, becomes: He said that they could go.
Now listen, and read along. Should people live on Mars?
Some scientists believe that people will live on Mars one day. But is it a good idea?
Arguments for: One space engineer told our class that Mars was the best planet for a human base.
She said it had water ice and that a day there was almost as long as a day on Earth.
Some people think exploring Mars will help us learn how life began.
Arguments against: A doctor said that the trip was very dangerous.
It takes about seven months to fly there, and astronauts would be far from help.
Also, building a base would be extremely expensive.
Some people say we should spend the money on problems on Earth.
Conclusion: Living on Mars is possible in the future, but it will be hard to survive there.
What do you think?
Another question. The video will stop. What did the space engineer say Mars had?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like discussion, argument, expensive.
You practised reported speech. And you read Should people live on Mars?
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!
